note: Per-system care lists for the Body wiki. Wording is our own and was reviewed line by line against MedlinePlus pages (National Library of Medicine); local items (TB two-week cough, floodwater within 24 to 48 hours, animal bites) follow Philippine DOH advice as reported and still need a DOH page cited by a person. 911 is the Philippine national emergency number. Lists only say when to get help: no doses, no home treatment, never wait and see.
checked: Most lines follow the sources below. A clinician has not signed them off.

emergency: Someone collapses and does not respond, or is not breathing or is only gasping
Chest pain, pressure, squeezing or tightness, even if it comes and goes or feels like heartburn
Pain or discomfort spreading to the arm, shoulder, back, neck, jaw or upper belly
Sudden shortness of breath, or a sudden cold sweat, nausea or faint feeling with no clear cause
Face drooping, arm or leg weakness, or slurred speech
Sudden confusion, trouble speaking or understanding, trouble seeing or walking, or a sudden severe headache
Passing out
Very high blood pressure with chest pain, breathlessness, weakness or trouble speaking
During dengue, or just after the fever ends: severe belly pain, vomiting 3 or more times in a day, bleeding from the nose or gums, blood in vomit or stool, or feeling tired, restless or irritable
doctor: Blood pressure above 180 on top or above 120 on the bottom, even with no symptoms: get care right away
Swollen feet or ankles, or quick weight gain
Out of breath on short walks or when lying flat
A racing, pounding or skipping heartbeat that keeps coming back
Blood pressure that stays above your target on several days
Dizziness when you stand up
prevention: Check your blood pressure often
Eat less salt, fried food and sweet drinks
Do not smoke, and walk 30 minutes most days
Take blood pressure medicine the way your doctor says

emergency: Trouble breathing that starts suddenly or is severe, or cannot speak a full sentence
Someone stops breathing
Blue or grey lips or face
The skin between the ribs or at the neck pulling in with each breath
Choking and cannot cough, speak or breathe
An asthma attack that does not ease with your reliever inhaler
Coughing up more than streaks of blood
Coughing up any blood with fever, chest pain, dizziness or trouble breathing
Chest pain with shortness of breath
Trouble breathing with sudden confusion or great sleepiness
doctor: A cough that lasts more than two weeks (it could be TB)
Blood in what you cough up: see a doctor right away
Night sweats and weight loss that you cannot explain
Fever with a cough, with or without mucus
Wheezing or breathlessness more often than usual
prevention: Do not smoke, and avoid smoky kitchens
Get the flu and pneumonia vaccines
Cover your cough and finish TB treatment
reported: A cough that lasts more than two weeks (it could be TB)

emergency: Face drooping, arm or leg weakness, or slurred speech
Sudden confusion, or trouble speaking or understanding
Sudden numbness on one side of the body
Sudden trouble seeing, walking, or keeping your balance
A sudden severe headache, or the worst headache of your life
A seizure that lasts more than 2 minutes, a first seizure, seizures one after another, or a seizure that is different from the person's usual ones
A seizure in water, or in someone who is pregnant, injured or has diabetes, or a seizure with trouble breathing or waking
A sudden high fever with a severe headache or a stiff neck

Head injury with passing out even briefly, vomiting more than once, confusion, great sleepiness, a seizure, a bad headache, unequal pupils, slurred speech, a weak or numb arm or leg, or heavy bleeding
Cannot be woken, or passing out
doctor: Headaches that are new or getting worse
Memory loss that gets in the way of daily life
Numb or tingling hands or feet that do not go away
Dizzy spells that keep coming back
Trouble sleeping for weeks
prevention: Control blood pressure and sugar
Sleep 7 to 8 hours and stay social
Wear a helmet, and do not drink and drive

illnesses: Diarrhea and typhoid from unsafe food or water
emergency: You vomit blood
Stools are black or bloody
Vomit that looks like coffee grounds
Sudden, sharp or severe belly pain, or a belly that is hard or very sore to touch
Severe belly pain with a high fever
Cannot pass stool or gas, especially with vomiting
Belly pain with chest, neck or shoulder pain, or trouble breathing
Pain between the shoulder blades with nausea
Belly pain after an injury, or if you could be pregnant
Yellow skin or eyes with confusion or being hard to wake
Vomiting or diarrhea that will not stop, with a very dry mouth, dizziness or hardly any urine
During dengue, or just after the fever ends: severe belly pain, vomiting 3 or more times in a day, bleeding from the nose or gums, blood in vomit or stool, or feeling tired, restless or irritable
Belly pain while you are being treated for cancer
doctor: Yellow skin or eyes
Belly pain that does not go away
Dark urine or pale stools
Diarrhea that lasts more than a few days
Fever with belly pain (it could be typhoid)
Cannot keep down any food or liquid
Trouble swallowing, or weight loss you cannot explain
prevention: Limit alcohol
Keep a healthy weight and move most days
Ask about the hepatitis B vaccine
Take medicines only as your doctor says

emergency: You cannot pass any urine
Severe pain in the side or back that will not ease, especially with vomiting
Fever with shaking chills and back or side pain
Swollen body with shortness of breath or chest pain
Confusion or great sleepiness with very little urine
Fever after wading in floodwater, with yellow skin, very little urine, bleeding or trouble breathing (severe leptospirosis)
doctor: Swollen feet or face
Much less urine, or foamy or bloody urine
Burning when you pass urine, or going very often
Waded in floodwater, even if you feel fine: go to a health center within 24 to 48 hours
Fever after floodwater with calf pain or red eyes: see a doctor right away
Pain in the side or back with a fever: see a doctor right away
prevention: Keep blood pressure and sugar in range
Drink water through the day, unless your doctor limits your fluids
Ask your doctor before using NSAID pain medicine or herbal products
reported: Fever after wading in floodwater, with yellow skin, very little urine, bleeding or trouble breathing (severe leptospirosis)
Waded in floodwater, even if you feel fine: go to a health center within 24 to 48 hours
Fever after floodwater with calf pain or red eyes: see a doctor right away

emergency: A bone sticking out of the skin, or a limb that looks bent or out of shape
Heavy bleeding
A fall or crash with neck or back pain, or numbness or weakness in the arms or legs (do not move the person)
Back pain with weak legs, numb groin or buttocks, or trouble holding urine or stool
Head injury with passing out even briefly, vomiting, confusion, great sleepiness, a seizure or a bad headache
Cannot stand or walk after a fall, or a possible broken hip, pelvis or thigh
A hand or foot below an injury that is pale, cold or blue
Chest pain, coughing blood, trouble breathing or fainting with a swollen leg (blood clot)
doctor: Pain, swelling or bruising after a fall (it could be broken): get care right away
A joint that is red, hot and very painful: see a doctor right away
Back pain that wakes you at night, or comes after a hard fall, or comes with fever or a history of cancer: see a doctor right away
Back pain that lasts more than 4 weeks
One leg swollen, red and sore: see a doctor right away (it could be a blood clot)
A bone that breaks from a small knock
prevention: Walk and do weight-bearing exercise most days
Eat foods with calcium and get some morning sun
Make floors and stairs safe from falls
Ask your doctor about a bone check after 50

illnesses: Hernia (a bulge where the wall is weak)
Muscle pain from some cholesterol medicine
emergency: Chest pressure or pain, with or without a cold sweat, or pain spreading to the arm or jaw
Sudden weakness in the face, an arm or a leg on one side
A hernia bulge that is painful and will not go back, or turns red, purple or dark, or comes with vomiting, fever, or no gas or stool
Severe muscle pain with dark, red or cola-colored urine
A swollen, red, warm leg with sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, coughing blood or fainting
After an injury: a very tight, swollen arm or leg, or severe pain that pain medicine does not ease
Jaw stiffness or muscle spasms after a wound
doctor: One calf or thigh swollen, red and warm: see a doctor right away (it could be a blood clot)
Muscle pain or weakness after starting a new medicine
A bulge in the belly or groin
Weakness that is getting worse over weeks
A muscle that stays swollen or bruised after an injury
prevention: Walk a little every day
Eat enough protein such as fish, egg and beans
Warm up before heavy work, and do not lift heavy loads alone
Drink enough water, unless your doctor limits your fluids

emergency: Passing out, a seizure, or being very confused or hard to wake, especially with diabetes
Low sugar signs that do not get better after something sweet
With diabetes: fruity breath, fast deep or hard breathing, vomiting, or being less alert
Severe pain in the upper belly, often going to the back, or with vomiting
With an overactive thyroid: a racing heart with fever, confusion, agitation or shaking
doctor: Very thirsty, urinating often, or blurry vision
Cuts or sores that heal slowly, or tingling feet
Sugar readings that are often above your target
Shaky, sweaty spells that keep coming back (low sugar)
A lump or swelling at the front of the neck
Racing heart and weight loss, or always cold, tired and gaining weight
prevention: Keep a healthy weight and move daily
Eat less sugar and smaller rice portions
Use iodized salt
Never stop steroid medicine suddenly

emergency: Swelling of the face, eyes, lips or tongue, trouble breathing or swallowing, a hoarse voice, or hives with dizziness or fainting
A burn the size of your palm or larger, a deep burn, a blistered burn on the face, hands, feet or groin, or a burn from chemicals or electricity
Breathed in smoke from a fire
Red, painful skin that spreads quickly
Purple or dark red spots that do not fade when pressed, with fever
Painful blisters or peeling skin over the body after starting a new medicine
Snake bite
Spreading redness or red streaks with a high fever, drowsiness or looking very sick
A burn and you are not sure how bad it is, or a burn with pale, clammy skin or fainting
Very hot after sun or hard work, with confusion, odd behavior, slurred speech, a seizure or passing out (heat stroke)
An animal bite that is deep or large, shows muscle or bone, is on the head, face or neck, or bleeds heavily
doctor: A mole that changes shape, color or size
A wound that does not heal in weeks
A boil that is growing, very painful or leaking pus
A rash that spreads, or itching that lasts for weeks
A dark streak under a nail
Red, warm, swollen skin: see a doctor right away
Dog or cat bite or scratch: go to an animal bite center right away, or an emergency room if it is closed
prevention: Bathe and dry well, especially in the folds
Use sunscreen and a hat in strong sun
Do not share towels, and clean small cuts
reported: Dog or cat bite or scratch: go to an animal bite center right away, or an emergency room if it is closed
